Rep. Gill Announces 2026 Academy Appointees | Representative Brandon Gill Skip to main content Phone:  (202) 225-7772 Email Me Address:  1305 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Rep. Gill Announces 2026 Academy Appointees June 2, 2026 Press Release Flower Mound, TX — Congressman Brandon Gill (R-TX) today announced the students from the 26th Congressional District who have accepted appointments to attend military service academies.  One of the privileges of serving in the U.S. House of Representatives is the opportunity to nominate superlative young people to be considered for appointment to the U.S. Military Academy at West Point, NY, the U.S. Naval Academy at Annapolis, MD, the U.S. Air Force Academy at Colorado Springs, CO, and the U.S. Merchant Marine Academy at Kings Point, NY. The U.S. Coast Guard Academy at New London, CT, does not require a congressional nomination. This past November, the 26th Congressional District Academy Board, chaired by Mr. Paul Cristina, met to complete an objective, merit-based review of applicants’ files and to conduct personal interviews. Following the Board’s work, Congressman Gill’s staff submitted the TX-26 nomination slates to the service academies for appointment consideration.  The incoming Class of 2030 service academy appointees were honored at a reception hosted by the City of The Colony. Mayor Richard Boyer welcomed the appointees, their families, and members of the 26th Congressional District Academy Board. The colors were presented by the American Legion Holley-Riddle Post 21 Honor Guard.  At the reception, each appointee in attendance was presented with a  Special Certificate of Congressional Recognition  and a flag flown over the U.S. Capitol at the request of Congressman Gill in honor of their appointments. These appointees reside in the 26th Congressional District and received a nomination from Congressman Gill, Senator Cruz, or a military-affiliated nomination. Gill Introduces Bill to Protect American Homebuyers | Representative Brandon Gill Skip to main content Phone:  (202) 225-7772 Email Me Address:  1305 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Rep. Gill Introduces Bill to Protect American Homebuyers June 29, 2026 Press Release Washington, D.C. —  Congressman Brandon Gill (TX-26) today introduced the Homeownership Eligibility Reform Act  to restrict eligibility for Federal Housing Administration (FHA)-insured mortgages and Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) securitized mortgages to only U.S. citizens. The legislation builds on HUD’s action  that limited FHA eligibility to U.S. citizens and lawful permanent residents by establishing a citizenship requirement in statute. Specifically, the bill would prohibit noncitizens from receiving FHA-backed financing and prohibits the FHFA (Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac) from purchasing or securitizing conventional mortgages on family homes when the borrower is not a U.S. citizen. “The American housing market is failing American buyers—we’re seeing this in my district in North Texas and across the country. The home price-to-income ratio has nearly doubled in the last 50 years, with the average first-time homebuyer now at a record-high 40 years old,” said Rep. Gill. “Taxpayer-backed mortgage programs exist to help Americans, not subsidize aliens competing in an already unaffordable market. My bill works in lockstep with President Trump’s policies to reduce demand, lower costs, and put American homebuyers first.” It is becoming increasingly difficult for Americans to purchase homes, something many consider to be a core component of the American dream and families’ primary financial asset. Housing market pressures are exacerbated in part by foreigners taking advantage of FHA loans  to buy houses with little money down, increasing the demand for housing and making home ownership inaccessible for many Americans, particularly young first-time homebuyers. Gill Bill Enforces English Language Proficiency for All | Representative Brandon Gill Skip to main content Phone:  (202) 225-7772 Email Me Address:  1305 Longworth House Office Building Washington, DC 20515 Rep. Gill Bill Enforces English Language Proficiency for All July 16, 2026 Press Release Washington, D.C. —  Congressman Brandon Gill (TX-26) today introduced the English Language Proficiency Act  to rescind the English proficiency and civics examination exceptions from U.S. naturalization law. The bill holds every citizenship applicant, regardless of age, to the same standard of understanding the English language, history, principles, and form of government of the United States. “English is the common tongue that holds American communities together,” said Rep Gill.  “It is of paramount importance that every American citizen be able to communicate in the same language. My bill holds everyone to the same standard already on the books, restoring equal treatment under nationalization law.” Congress has tested newcomers' civic attachment since the Naturalization Act of 1802, which required aliens seeking citizenship to demonstrate good moral character and loyalty to the Constitution. Current law carves out an exception that lets certain elderly aliens skip the English proficiency and civics exams that every other applicant must pass. Rep. Gill’s English Language Proficiency Act repeals the age-based exemptions, closing the carve-out for good. The bill adds no new naturalization requirements. It simply holds every applicant to the same standard already on the books. Cosponsors (3): Reps. Randy Fine, Barry Moore, Beth Van Duyne Supporting Groups:  Immigration Accountability Project, Pro English Background:   Non-English speakers at home nearly tripled over the last three decades, climbing from 23.1 million to 67.8 million people, or roughly one in five Americans, according to Census Bureau data cited by the State Department. Gill and Correa Introduce Deputy Darren Almendarez Act July 23, 2026 Press Release Washington, D.C. —  Congressman Brandon Gill (TX-26) today introduced the Deputy Darren Almendarez Act , a bipartisan effort to crack down on catalytic converter theft. The legislation would make it a federal crime to knowingly possess, purchase, or sell a catalytic converter that has been unlawfully removed from a motor vehicle when the conduct affects interstate or foreign commerce. Violators would be subject to fines of up to $100,000 and imprisonment for up to five years, with enhanced penalties for repeat offenders. Congressman Lou Correa (D-CA) is the colead on this legislation. “Catalytic converter theft has imposed significant costs on families, businesses, and law enforcement agencies across the country,” said Rep. Gill.  “By targeting the black market for stolen catalytic converters, this legislation aims to disrupt the financial incentive behind these thefts. It is a tragedy that Deputy Sheriff Almendarez lost his life because of the crime this bill aims to prevent. My prayers are with his family.” The legislation is named in honor of Deputy Sheriff Darren Almendarez , a Harris County Deputy, who was shot and killed while off duty when he attempted to stop three men who were stealing a catalytic converter. A similar bill named after Deputy Darren Almendarez became law  in Texas, and this legislation builds on that model at the federal level. The legislation includes carve-outs for legitimate activities including: Vehicle owners or lessees removing converters from their own vehicles;  Manufacturers, dealers, and repair facilities acting within their official duties; Licensed and regulated recycling entities, salvage yards, law enforcement, educational programs, and other specified organizations “California leads the nation in catalytic converter thefts.
